findings.summary: Shard 3's runner booted zero microVMs (5/5 `izba run` attempts, first attempt onward, empty guest console) and the harness destroyed the only evidence that could name why, twice: (a) `--action-timeout-s 120` equals `IZBA_BOOT_TIMEOUT_SECS: '120'`, so izba is SIGKILLed at the exact instant it would print `did not become healthy within 120s; check <console.log>` — the diagnostic is structurally unobservable; (b) `_console_tails` tails only logs/console.log, which is EMPTY when the VMM fails below the guest, while cloud-hypervisor's own stderr sits unmentioned in the sibling logs/vmm.log. Fix: action timeout > boot budget; tail vmm.log too; add a one-shot boot preflight so a KVM-less runner fails loudly instead of emitting five silent 120s timeouts that read like a product hang. Files: .github/workflows/dogfood.yml:293,411; hack/dogfood/oracles.py (_console_tails).

findings.summary: `izba run <name> -- apk add curl && curl -v https://example.com/` has its `&&` consumed by the HARNESS's host shell, so the decisive fetch ran on the CI runner, not in the sandbox — proven by the certificate chain in that action's own stderr (`CAfile: /etc/ssl/certs/ca-certificates.crt` + Cloudflare issuer, vs `/etc/izba/ca-bundle.pem` on every genuine in-guest fetch) and by izba netlog containing no example.com row at all. It produced a decisive functional red on a promise that was never probed. Add the rule to the Actor's operating notes (everything after `--` must be one `sh -c '…'`), and/or classify an unquoted `&&`/`;` after `izba run|exec … --` as self-inflicted rather than functional. File: hack/dogfood/run_journeys.py.

findings.summary: `deep-exception-does-not-follow-a-raw-address` declares `expect_stdout_re 'DENY\s+l[37]\s.*:443'`, but no anchor promises a DENY: a raw-IP dial to an ALLOW-LISTED host on an always-inspected port is terminated at L7 and authorized by name, so the correct observable is `ALLOW l7 example.com:443 GET /` (izba's own certificate). DP-2 promises only 'no snoop record ⇒ no passthrough', i.e. not SPLICED. As written the journey would manufacture a false security red from correct behaviour; it escaped only because the Actor pinned an IPv6 literal in an IPv4-only guest and the connection never left the sandbox (`Immediate connect fail … Network unreachable`, curl exit 7, zero example.com rows in netlog). Fix: assert `ALLOW l7\s.*example\.com:443`, force an IPv4 literal (getent ahostsv4), and rename the journey to name the real rule (the hatch follows the DNS-snoop binding, not the literal). File: dogfood-pt2/tier-deep.json.

findings.summary: The e3e7d78e GUI settle fix is only half-effective: `--max-turns 18` counts `read` observations as turns (run_gui_journeys.py:750, `turns += 1` before every next_command, and a `read` reply `continue`s), and the new 'look again if it is not ready yet' instruction spends them. `gui-removing-the-exempt-port-unlocks-the-row` ended mid-step-1 after 8 actions plus ~10 reads with `● unsaved changes` on screen and managed policy.yaml byte-unchanged, so the unlock-after-removing-the-pinned-port escape valve is unverified this run. (It also mis-clicked `@e25` = 'Remove port 80' instead of the pinned 443, which alone would have blocked the rename.) Cap reads separately from turns, or raise --max-turns for GUI journeys needing >=5 interactions per step; the sibling journeys that finished needed 10-11 actions. Files: hack/dogfood/gui/run_gui_journeys.py:750; .github/workflows/dogfood.yml:551.

findings.summary: Every datapath journey grades the passthrough on `izba netlog --summary`, whose `l3` tier alone cannot distinguish a pinning splice from an ordinary tier-2 allow — an oracle that could credit the hatch for the wrong mechanism. The discriminator exists and was never asked for: a splice audits with the rule string `passthrough (protocol: tcp)` (mitm_runtime.rs:367), rendered only by the non-summary `izba netlog <name>`. Assert on that line. This is the harness half of predicted flag F6. File: dogfood-pt2/tier-deep.json.

findings.summary: Coverage, not product: shard 3 booted zero microVMs, so `deep-two-hosts-one-port-only-one-passes-through` (the ONLY journey covering InspectionTable's per-host passthrough set vs its policy-global inspected port set — 'an explicit tcp entry does not remove its own port from the inspected set') and `deep-seeding-from-observed-traffic-keeps-the-declaration` verified nothing. The latter is counted as this tier's one collapsed positive: `izba policy enable seeded` reported 'added 0 observed endpoint(s)', so the observed-traffic mutator ran against an empty set and its two core steps passed on assertions a no-op satisfies. Re-dispatch both; tighten the seeding assertion to require `added [1-9]`.

findings.summary: Coverage, not product: three deep promises were never exercised for Actor-side reasons and should be re-run with tightened steps — (1) 'a dormant hatch really stays intercepted' (the decisive fetch ran on the host, see the host-shell finding); (2) 'the declaration applies without a restart' (the Actor used `--rm`, so `izba policy reload live-pin` and `izba netlog live-pin` both correctly answered 'no such sandbox'); (3) the GUI 'removing the exempt port unlocks the row' escape valve (turn starvation).
